mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is already high (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when the contraction is due to temporary weather events.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI inflation) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12-mo MA in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies rise together, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is not robust during housing-specific supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a labor market expansion without wage inflation, which supports corporate margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA and UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp) for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market expansion with low wage pressure
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such episodes, or the effect reverses when wage growth accelerates (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a flat or declining consumption series (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA for 4 consecutive months and GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes, or the effect is absent when savings are driven by precautionary motives during a crisis.
